Topics include an early history of Computer Science, a study of the people who shaped Computer Science, and a discussion of major milestones in Computer Science. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.

beats.narration: Now define Prerequisites & Course Restrictions precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Students cannot take and receive credit for this course if they have credit for CSCI-471. beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Early History of Computer Science operates in a concrete sequence. Students who have a background in Computer Science theories, algorithms, and data structures will be provided a look at the history of Computer Science from historical and current perspectives. Consider this worked case: Students will examine early computing devices and their evolution to understand how historical milestones shape modern designs. On screen, present a timeline graphic showing key early computing devices and their chronological progression. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a timeline graphic showing key early computing devices and their chronological progression.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in People Who Shaped Computer Science and make the decision criteria explicit. Additionally, students will study current issues in Computer Science, including legal, ethical, diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility and privacy issues, and how past issues affect modern designs and decision making by computer scientists. Consider this worked case: Students will profile key historical figures and analyze their specific roles in advancing computer science. On screen, display a collage of portraits of influential computer scientists with brief biographical notes. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: People Who Shaped Computer Science
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a collage of portraits of influential computer scientists with brief biographical notes.

beats.narration: Apply Major Milestones in Computer Science to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. They should respect privacy. Consider this worked case: Students will map major technological breakthroughs to understand how past issues affect modern designs and decision making by computer scientists. On screen, show a flowchart connecting major milestones to their impact on contemporary computing practices. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a flowchart connecting major milestones to their impact on contemporary computing practices.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Current Issues: Legal & Ethical Frameworks, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Consider this worked case: Students will review the ACM Code of Ethics to identify how computing professionals should avoid harm and be honest and trustworthy. On screen, display the ACM Code of Ethics principles as a set of icons with corresponding text summaries. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display the ACM Code of Ethics principles as a set of icons with corresponding text summaries.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Current Issues: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Accessibility with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations. Consider this worked case: Students will analyze case studies showing how historical biases influenced modern accessibility standards in software development. On screen, present a Venn diagram overlapping 'Past Issues' and 'Modern Designs' with 'Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility' in the intersection. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Present a Venn diagram overlapping 'Past Issues' and 'Modern Designs' with 'Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility' in the intersection.

beats.narration: Use Current Issues: Privacy & Security to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Consider this worked case: Students will evaluate a scenario where a software update must balance user privacy with system security requirements. On screen, show a lock-and-shield icon representing privacy and security, with a checklist of ethical computing decision steps. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a lock-and-shield icon representing privacy and security, with a checklist of ethical computing decision steps.

beats.narration: Connect Responsible Technical Communication to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Consider this worked case: Students will draft a research abstract that clearly separates claims from evidence and cites prior work. On screen, display a side-by-side comparison of a 'misleading conclusion' vs. an 'accurate result' report with annotations. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a side-by-side comparison of a 'misleading conclusion' vs. an 'accurate result' report with annotations.

beats.narration: Finish with Research Integrity & Problem-Solving Methods as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Consider this worked case: Students will practice identifying potential conflicts of interest and disclose them according to publication policy. On screen, show a checklist graphic listing 'Avoid plagiarism', 'Disclose conflicts', and 'Maintain high standards' as research integrity steps. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.

beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a checklist graphic listing 'Avoid plagiarism', 'Disclose conflicts', and 'Maintain high standards' as research integrity steps.

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
sources.title: ACM Publications Policies
